question: Is the current Python resemblance encoder cost intrinsic to the depth-1 relation mechanism, or implementation debt?
control: A small native C implementation of the exact resemblance.delta_encode semantics was compared byte-for-byte with the Python encoder on deterministic 1 MiB controls. Payload identity was exact before timing.
interpretation: Python byte-wise delta construction is implementation debt, not a fundamental mechanism cost.
Small local edits can be encoded in roughly 2 ms by a native exact implementation on this local court.
Large-churn relations still cost tens of milliseconds and need product-level admission/runtime measurement.
Highly compressible data remains an economics edge case: the relation may save very few bytes even when native encoding is fast, so direct fallback/admission must consider absolute benefit.
decision: Do not reject Issue26 reference deltas because the current Python research encoder is slow. A product prototype should bind an exact native/memory-safe encoder or equivalent accelerated path and retain direct ordinary fallback. This is implementation feasibility evidence only, not product timing credit.
